topic.title: Rich vs poor: what each does with a ₹20,000 raise

title: Rich vs Poor: your ₹20,000 raise 💸
description:
Same raise, two very different lives. Which one are you?
Illustrative only. Not financial advice.
cta: Rich move or poor move? Tell me below

lines.text: Poor guy gets ₹20,000 more salary. Rich guy gets the same raise.
Same raise. I invest all of it. Every single month.
10 years at 12% a year, and that raise becomes ₹46.5 L.
Your phone? Old in two years. Worth almost nothing.
Spend it, and the raise is gone. Invest it, and it becomes ₹46.5 L.
Same raise. Two lives. So, next time a poor guy gets a raise...

notes: 14 figures computed from inputs; 8 cross-checked against closed-form formulas.

India Short, no sourced facts. Inputs realistic: a 16% consumer loan for a phone over 2 years (Indian personal and consumer-durable loans run about 12-24%); 12% a year assumed for an equity SIP, stated on screen as an assumption. A phone losing most of its value in two years is a fair, hedged claim ('almost nothing'). No product or fund named, no advice; description carries the disclaimer.
